Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
952 PM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
While trends continue toward a less impactful system Sunday 
into Monday, gale watches have been issued for portions of the 
ocean waters for Sunday night. Trends also favor a significant
coastal storm from Wednesday night through Friday.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Low pressure moving up the coast will impact the area with
rain Sunday afternoon into Monday morning. Localized minor
coastal impacts are possible due to approaching full moon on 
Tuesday.

2) Another coastal storm is likely from Wednesday night into
Friday with heavy rain, strong easterly winds, and widespread 
coastal flooding.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Low pressure several hundred miles E of Florida will move N and
slowly intensify as it moves past Cape Hatteras Sunday morning,
then passes very near the area Sunday night. Uncertainty on 
exact low track increases on Sunday, with the ECMWF east and 
showing very little impact to the area, 12Z REFS/HRRR farther 
west with the low crossing Long Island and rain/wind impact 
farther west into the area, and the GFS in between. Due to the 
uncertainty siding with the middle ground GFS-like solution,
with a somewhat stronger low passing just SE of Long Island. 
This still maintains a fair amt of rainfall west of the low 
track especially across Long Island and S CT, but a more limited 
wind impact. 

Some light rain could arrive as early as late morning or early
afternoon Sunday, then rain should pick up in intensity late day
Sunday into Sunday evening, with the rain moderate to heavy at
times. A few tstms remain possible across ern Long Island and 
SE CT Sunday evening just E of the low track. 

Current forecast calls for a widespread 1-2 inch rainfall mainly
across S CT and Long Island, but also clipping NYC with about an
inch. Amts north/west drop off to 1/2 to 3/4 inch well
north/west. Localized totals closer to 3 inches still possible
across eastern Long Island/SE CT, with the 12Z REFS showing a 
slight chance of 2 inches in 3 hr across SE CT late Sunday 
evening. This is conditional on the low taking a track similar
to the GFS. 

Wind impact Sunday night will depend on the track of the sfc 
low. Generally anticipating winds to increase out of the E as 
the low approaches the area with sustained wind 10-15 mph and 
gusts upwards of 25-30 mph possible along the coast. There is a 
low chance for a brief period of gusts 40-45 mph out of the SE-S
out east if the low tracks close enough to the area. 

The coastal flood threat continues to look minimal at best with
this system as the highest surge will be Sunday night, during 
the time of the lower of the two high tide cycles. Even the
western Sound, which should see the better surge, should fall
short. Winds will then shift around to the N-NW late Sunday
night, becoming more westerly for Monday, lowering water 
levels. A few Long Island south shore back bay locations,
particularly along the south shore of Nassau, could see water
levels getting close to minor flood benchmarks Monday morning
due to some earlier tidal piling. However, confidence is low,
and any flooding would be localized. The progressive nature of
the storm is another limiting factor. 

.KEY MESSAGE 2...
Models continue to agree on a potentially large, impactful
coastal low pressure system impacting the area Wednesday night
into Thanksgiving Day and Friday. This system has the potential
to be more impactful regarding wind and coastal flooding than 
the system moving through on Sunday into Monday. Many locations
need less than a foot to reach minor coastal flood benchmarks
due to high astronomical tides associated with the new moon on
Tue. The way it stands, the current forecast supports widespread
minor to moderate flooding, perhaps even localized major. In 
addition beach flooding, erosion, and overwash would all be on 
the table. 

Also worth noting is that while most models have some sort of
large low pressure system, the mid and upper level pattern is 
complex enough where any subtle change can result in large 
differences in intensity, track, and timing. At this time, it is
something to keep monitoring.

&&

.AVIATION /03Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
High pressure remains in control through tonight. Low pressure
approaches from the south on Sunday.

MVFR or lower conditions are possible overnight, especially
along the coast, where low level moisture is increasing.
Question is how long this lasts as high clouds are expected to 
lower and thicken, which would eventually allow lower levels to 
warm and thus allow conditions to improve. Best chances for MVFR
or lower are at KGON, KISP, and KBDR. It is uncertain whether 
these conditions make their way into the metro terminals, but 
the highest chances exist for KJFK. Once high clouds thicken
enough, fog and low stratus becomes less likely until Sunday 
morning into the afternoon with all terminals likely at IFR by 
00Z Mon with the approach of the low. Showers possible in the 
morning, then rain likely in the afternoon. 

Winds becoming light and variable overnight. Winds then pick up
on Sunday from the ENE-NE at 10 to 15 kt in the afternoon with 
gusts 15 to around 20 kt by late afternoon.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Timing of lowering flight categories on Sunday could be a few
hours off, occurring several hours earlier than what is
forecast.

.OUTLOOK FOR 00Z Monday through Thursday... 

Sunday Night: Conditions improving by around daybreak Monday. NW
winds 5-10 kt with gusts  15-20 kt. 

Monday: VFR. W-NW gusts 15-20 kt.

Tuesday: VFR. 

Wednesday: VFR. 

Wednesday night: VFR in the evening. E-NE winds gusts 20-30kt
with a chance of MVFR with rain late.

Thursday: Rain, IFR and LLWS likely. E-NE winds potentially
gusting 35-45kt.


Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Low pressure moving up the coast will likely produce SCA 
conditions on the near shore ocean waters by late Sunday
afternoon, and to all waters Sunday night. Depending on exact
low track, the near shore ocean waters E of Moriches and most 
of the outer ocean waters could see a period of SE-S gales 
Sunday night, but this remains uncertain enough that a gale
watch and not a warning has been issued for that time frame. 

Residual hazardous ocean seas likely to persist into Mon night,
with only a brief lull possible on the near shore ocean waters
for Tue afternoon and night before winds and seas ramp up on 
Wed with the approach of low pressure from the S, interacting
with strong high pressure to the north to produce strong E-NE
winds. On the ocean, gusts 25-30 kt likely to return by Wed
afternoon, ramping up to gale force by Wed night and to storm 
force on Thu. Gale force wind gusts should arrive to the non
ocean waters by late Wed night and continue into Thu. Max
significant wave heights should ramp up to at least 12-20 ft on
the ocean and occasionally to 20-25 ft out east, 7-10 ft on
western Block Island Sound E of Orient Point, and 4-6 ft on 
Long Island Sound as well as the entrance to NY Harbor.
